source: Process agents' design notes of 1 October: handoff/design-notes/white-label.yaml, ticketing-guest.yaml and finance-insights.yaml (corrections); WEB-001, GST-001, GST-047, WEB-029, KSK-002 corrections
what: getTenantConfig (brand, theme, fonts, header, footer, navigation, homepage) needs a guest or a staff session, so a first-time visitor's storefront (WEB-001, GST-001, the maintenance and sold-out pages, the kiosk) cannot load the tenant's brand before anyone signs in; KSK-002 cited TENANT_CONFIGURE.
decision: A dedicated public read, additive to the white-label contract: getPublishedTenantConfig, GET /storefront/tenant-config, audience anonymous, guest and device, security optional (`{}` or guestAuth), no permission, tenant scope, offline-capable and cacheable at the edge. The tenant is resolved from the request's host at the edge (tenancy.resolveTenantHost, SD-021): the verified custom domain or the platform subdomain, which is the tenant slug the app and kiosk builds use; an unknown host is 404. Optional venueId resolves the booking-flow display settings with that venue's overrides (CFG-11). It returns PublishedTenantConfig: the published version and date, brand, app icons, theme, fonts, header, footer, navigation, homepage, booking-flow display settings, languages, accessibility, the enabled module and feature keys, and the live maintenance, sold-out, minimum-app-version and contact status. Draft markers, notification branding, enabled payment methods, licensing and the CMS status fields are left out. getTenantConfig is unchanged; its description points visitors to the new read. WEB-001, GST-001 and KSK-002 call it instead of getTenantConfig.
applied: contracts/satellite/white-label.yaml (path /storefront/tenant-config, schema PublishedTenantConfig); WEB-001, GST-001, KSK-002; the WEB-001 and KSK-002 steps of flows F01, F07 and F75; the lineage entry; tools/applied/guest-screen-fixes-2-october.py

source: Process agents' design notes of 1 October: handoff/design-notes/white-label.yaml, ticketing-guest.yaml and finance-insights.yaml (corrections); WEB-045, GST-040, GST-057 corrections
what: listPolicies is staff-only (TENANT_CONFIGURE), so no guest could read the terms, privacy, refund, cookie or accessibility policy (WEB-045, GST-040, the checkout T&Cs); listFaqs and listContentPages need a guest session, so help told a visitor to sign in.
decision: Three public reads, additive, shaped like GFIX-1 (audience anonymous, guest and device; security optional; no permission; tenant from the host; cacheable): listPublishedPolicies, GET /storefront/policies (optional kind; the current version of each published PolicyKind as PublishedPolicy, bounded at five); listPublishedFaqs, GET /storefront/faqs (PublishedFaqCategory, published entries only); listPublishedContentPages, GET /storefront/pages (optional categoryCode and slug, cursor-paged, PublishedContentPage, published and enabled pages only, ordered by sortOrder then slug). None returns a partition key or a person. The staff reads are unchanged. WEB-045 and GST-040 read all three, GST-057 reads the pages (category fixed by the screen), and the checkout T&Cs on WEB-012 and GST-009 read the terms; the help and accessibility screens' no-access state is public.
applied: contracts/satellite/white-label.yaml (paths /storefront/policies, /storefront/faqs, /storefront/pages; schemas PublishedPolicy, PublishedFaqCategory, PublishedContentPage); WEB-045, GST-040, GST-057, WEB-012, GST-009; the lineage entries

source: Process agents' design notes of 1 October: handoff/design-notes/white-label.yaml, ticketing-guest.yaml and finance-insights.yaml (corrections)
what: The guest web, app and kiosk screens still carried the 9 September generator's output: query parameters as text fields (Venue id, Kind, Is sellable, Principal id, Shift id, Status, Created from/to, Outlet id, Category id, Active at, As at, Purpose, Category code, Slug), responses as 'Every ...' tables with plumbing and staff columns (scopePath, principal ids, venueId, isDraft, the CMS counts), buttons named after operationIds with modals collecting the raw request body (Evaluate promotions, Create order, Create payment, Acquire inventory hold, Create seat hold, Store payment token, the kiosk's eight CreatePaymentRequest fields), the staff order list (listOrders) beside the guest's own, staff CRM fields (engagement score, lifetime value, tags) on Home, and 'Transfer order tickets' as the primary action on payment, confirmation, membership and kiosk screens.
decision: Removed from the guest screens named in the notes' corrections, each screen keeping its guest behaviour. Staff filters go (the venue comes from the session); raw tables become guest card lists with guest columns, or go where another component already shows the data; staff and plumbing columns are stripped from every component on those screens; raw forms go and the operation moves behind the guest action (one Pay, a tap on a seat, a quantity stepper, promotions evaluated by themselves into the near-miss banner, a once-asked eligibility declaration, the gateway's card form, a payment-terminal prompt on the kiosk). Rebound: listOrders to listMyOrders (WEB-030, GST-014), getGuestProfile to getMyProfile (GST-001), the kiosk's transfer to reprintOrder (KSK-009, KSK-010, KSK-012). Taken off, each recorded as a removed gap on its screen: transferOrderTickets from WEB-012, WEB-013, WEB-019, WEB-023, GST-009, GST-010 and GST-019; listOrders where listMyOrders was already declared (WEB-019, GST-019) or the screen opens on one order (GST-018); listGuestMemberships (WEB-022, WEB-023, GST-015); claimTicketTransfer from the sender's WEB-030 (GST-014 keeps it, from the link); addCartLine from GST-009; checkoutCart and createPayment from the parking screens (WEB-041, GST-027: parking is paid in the basket, R166, so F50's payment step moves to GST-009); listCatalogueBundles from GST-056; createReferral and getMyChallenges from GST-072. createCart stays on WEB-010, its only caller, as the runtime's background call rather than a button. Corrections that are not about staff content (missing frames, navigation gaps, enum contradictions, operations that do not exist yet) stay with the lead as change requests.
applied: screens/P01-guest-web-storefront.yaml, P02-guest-mobile-app.yaml and P05-guest-kiosk.yaml by tools/applied/guest-screen-fixes-2-october.py; flows F50, F55, F57 and F75

source: Process agents' design notes of 1 October: handoff/design-notes/white-label.yaml, ticketing-guest.yaml and finance-insights.yaml (corrections); GST-001, GST-038, GST-040, GST-057, KSK-002, GST-019, WEB-045 corrections
what: Guest screens named a staff permission as their no-access state ('Shown when the caller lacks PRODUCT_VIEW ... and names that permission', GUEST_VIEW on Home, TENANT_CONFIGURE on help), and the web help centre said 'Sign in to see this'.
decision: No guest screen names a permission (ADR-0025). Guest web and app screens take the signed-in guest's state (not signed in: offered sign-in and brought back; not theirs: said without saying whose). Screens that read only published content (help, accessibility, contact, maintenance and sold out) are public and have no no-access case. The kiosk holds no permission and needs none; a revoked kiosk goes out of service (KSK-014). Applied to every P01, P02 and P05 screen whose no-access state named a permission or asked a visitor to sign in to read help.
applied: emptyNoAccess on the screens listed, by tools/applied/guest-screen-fixes-2-october.py

source: Typed checks of the council of 2 October (branch change-rules): tools/check-audience-match.py AM-GUEST-SECURITY and tools/check-preauth-session.py PS-LOAD-NEEDS-SESSION
what: 84 operations declared a guest audience while their security admitted only a staff bearer token (most fell back to their contract's default), so a guest screen calling one was refused; and 200 loads on the 125 guest screens a visitor reaches before signing in needed a session, led by listProducts (25 screens), getWaitTimes (14), listPerformances (9) and getAvailability (9).
decision: Widening only, so every client built against r1 keeps working. 29 published, non-personal reads a first-time visitor needs (the catalogue, availability, performances, seats, offers, the shop, queues, programmes and rewards on offer, consent purposes, an anonymous visitor's recommendations, the module catalogue) take `security: [{}, guestAuth, bearerAuth]`; 51 other guest operations (the guest's own records and actions) take `[guestAuth, bearerAuth]`, so personal reads stay behind sign-in. A second pass adds `{}` to 20 published reads that already admitted a guest token but no visitor (wait times, the guest menu and dining, the venue map, transport timetables and fares, parking facilities, tender exchange rates, the storefront's analytics tags). The four operations whose only non-staff audience is `public` (an external reviewer or a TICVAI prospect: decideApprovalRequest, listApprovalRequests, listVenueTypeTemplates, submitOnboardingApplication) are left for the lead. check-contract-compat now counts a security list that only gained alternatives as additive.

source: tools/check-preauth-session.py PS-UNDECLARED-SIGNIN and the PS-LOAD-NEEDS-SESSION findings left after GFIX-5
what: 51 loads of the guest's own records on screens a visitor can reach (tickets, orders, wallet, memberships, reservations, cases, notifications, loyalty, queue place, saved routes) did not say the screen is behind sign-in, and personal loads on public screens did not say they wait for one.
decision: Screens that are the guest's own record declare `subjectId` `from: session` (behind sign-in; a visitor is offered sign-in and brought back, GFIX-4). On public screens a personal load says it runs only when signed in; on booking, basket and kiosk screens the cart, hold or order read says it rides on the guest session the device holds, signed in or the anonymous cart session (ADR-0045).
